basis: Carcinoma originates in the ectocervix, a reproductive organ outside the 13 axes.
Invasive urothelial carcinoma originates in the bladder; the urinary tract belongs to the renal axis.
Inherited type I interferonopathy with inflammatory neurologic disease in the Aicardi-Goutieres spectrum; broader organ involvement is insufficiently established.
Clonal myeloid/lymphoid neoplasm of hematopoietic cells associated with JAK2 rearrangement; lymphoma is not universal across presentations.
Lesion directly affects the common fibular peripheral nerve.
Hereditary absence or abnormal development of cutaneous sweat glands causes generalized anhidrosis.
Congenital intestinal dysfunction causes malabsorptive diarrhea in 9/9; villous atrophy occurs in 3/9.
Primary pulmonary epithelial malignancy arising in the lung.
Congenital dyserythropoietic anemia; hepatic dysfunction supported by conjugated hyperbilirubinemia 8/8, elevated ALT 7/8 and AST 6/8; gallstones are separate.
Recurrent childhood encephalopathy with common ataxia and spasticity; joint hypermobility alone does not establish musculoskeletal damage.
CF, gastritis and megaloblastic anemia define syndrome; intellectual disability 80-99%. H. pylori infectious axis and renal involvement (30-79%) omitted at cap.
Progressive lower motor neuron degeneration; sustained denervation causes defining skeletal muscle atrophy and functional loss in most patients.
Becker nevus with defining ipsilateral muscular or skeletal hypoplasia; micromelia and shoulder muscle atrophy 80-99%. Breast abnormalities have no axis.
Hereditary motor axonal neuropathy; structural musculoskeletal involvement includes pes cavus 11/17 and flexion contractures 9/17; myopathic EMG only 3/12.
Defining cerebral and facial capillary malformations; ocular damage includes glaucoma and optic atrophy, each frequent (30-79%).
Childhood striatonigral neurodegeneration with progressive dystonia and loss of ambulation; postural changes and isolated CK elevation do not establish myopathy.
Acute leukemia defined by mixed-lineage hematopoietic blasts; the lymphoma ancestor does not establish a separate lymphoma or bone lesion.
Cutaneous meningioma occupies skin; meningioma histology does not require intracranial disease.
Mitochondrial defect; cardiomyopathy 2/2, thrombocytopenia 2/2, weakness 2/2 with elevated CK support heart, blood and muscle involvement. Alopecia 2/2 omitted at cap.
Intestinal secretion and absorption dysfunction defines the diarrhea; electrolyte disturbances are consequences rather than a defining metabolic disorder.
Skin fragility, atrophic scarring and generalized joint hypermobility define classic EDS; GI symptoms do not establish direct injury; aortic disease is occasional.
Intellectual disability, deafness and skeletal abnormalities define syndrome; persistent subcutaneous nodules and abnormal skin elasticity are frequent (30-79%).
Motor-sensory axonal neuropathy; distal amyotrophy 3/3 supports common muscle loss, with fatty replacement and structural foot deformities also reported.
Mitochondrial encephalopathy with lactic acidosis and hyperammonemia; hypertrophic cardiomyopathy 3/3. Renal tubular abnormalities lack frequency evidence.
GATA4-related atrioventricular septal malformation; pancreatic disease in the broader parent concept is not established for this subtype.
